discovery: The jamming transition: a unifying framework for rigidity and the onset of solidity in disordered matter
subfield: Soft condensed matter physics / physics of disordered systems
motivation: Liu and Nagel proposed that glasses, foams, emulsions, colloids and granular packings all become rigid through a common 'jamming' transition controlled by density, temperature and stress. Together with their collaborators they identified the critical point J, where soft frictionless spheres acquire rigidity at isostaticity. They showed that it has scale-free signatures: power-law scaling of pressure and shear modulus, excess contact number, a plateau of anomalous low-frequency vibrational modes, and diverging length scales. The framework made rigidity itself an object of statistical physics. It explains why amorphous solids differ fundamentally from crystals and has been confirmed in many experiments on suspensions, grains and foams. It underlies current understanding of shear thickening, yielding and rigidity percolation in biological tissue, and it inspired tunable and learning mechanical metamaterials. Few ideas have organised so much of everyday matter under one universal principle.
